x: Table names shorter than 3 characters are accepted (DynamoDB requires 3-255).

features.t: Items (put, get, update, delete, query, scan, batch, transactions)
x: Differential parity vs DynamoDB Local (tests/parity/ddb_differential.py, report in tests/parity/reports/): 149 of 152 hand-written cases (658 of 661 responses) and 400 of 400 random 30-operation sequences match; the 3 deviating cases are the TTL and CreateTable leniencies documented in this file.

features.t: Table class, deletion protection, encryption (at create)
x: Deletion protection is enforced (DeleteTable is rejected while it is on).

Provisioned capacity is ENFORCED: a per-table/GSI token bucket refilled at the provisioned rate with up to 300 seconds of burst (AWS's documented burst window) returns a real ProvisionedThroughputExceededException and publishes Read/WriteThrottleEvents + ThrottledRequests to CloudWatch; on-demand tables never throttle. Adaptive capacity and per-partition limits aren't modelled (the whole table is one bucket).
Expired items are removed when they are read, queried or scanned — not by a background process within ~48 hours as in AWS.

RestoreTableToPointInTime is enforced against the PITR window (rejected without PITR enabled, or for a RestoreDateTime outside [EarliestRestorableDateTime, LatestRestorableDateTime]) but always restores the table's current state — Vyomi keeps no change history, so every point in the window yields the same (latest) data.

CreateBackup writes the backup's table definition (backup-metadata.json) and every item as DynamoDB-JSON (data/1.json) into the simulator's own S3, in the visible bucket vyomi-dynamodb-backups under AWSDynamoDB/backups/<table>/<id>/. RestoreTableFromBackup reads those objects back, so deleting the S3 object makes the backup unusable (BackupNotFoundException) and DeleteBackup removes the objects. If no S3 store is wired the backup falls back to an in-store snapshot. BackupSizeBytes is the real size of the stored data.

Supported: SELECT (projection, WHERE with = <> < <= > >= BETWEEN IN AND/OR/NOT begins_with contains attribute_type size IS [NOT] MISSING, ? parameters, "table"."index"), INSERT ... VALUE (maps, lists, <<sets>>), UPDATE ... SET/REMOVE ... WHERE <full key> [AND condition], DELETE FROM ... WHERE <full key>.

CreateTable/UpdateTable StreamSpecification opens a real change-data-capture log per table: every PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem (including through BatchWriteItem/TransactWriteItems) appends a real stream record with the correct eventName (INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE) and NewImage/OldImage per StreamViewType; ListStreams/DescribeStream/GetShardIterator/GetRecords read it back with real sequence numbers and TRIM_HORIZON/LATEST/AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER/AFTER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER semantics.
Only ExportFormat=DYNAMODB_JSON and ExportType=FULL_EXPORT are implemented (Amazon Ion and incremental exports are rejected with ValidationException).

ImportTable reads real bytes from the S3 store and really creates and populates a new table: CSV and DYNAMODB_JSON (the exact newline-delimited shape ExportTableToPointInTime writes, so export+import is a genuine round trip) with NONE or GZIP compression.

EnableKinesisStreamingDestination requires the named stream to really exist in Vyomi's own Kinesis core (core/kinesis_core.py) and rejects it with ResourceNotFoundException otherwise; once enabled, every item write/delete publishes a real change-data-capture record into that stream (readable back with GetRecords) — not stored config.

PutResourcePolicy validates the document (valid JSON, at least one Allow/Deny statement with a Principal), tracks a real RevisionId for optimistic concurrency (ExpectedRevisionId is enforced on Put and Delete), and rejects a policy granting '*' access unless ConfirmRemoveSelfResourceAccess=true — the same guard real PutResourcePolicy applies. What is not modeled is runtime access evaluation: Vyomi has one implicit caller identity, so the policy content never actually denies or allows a specific request the way cross-account IAM evaluation would.

Every PutItem/GetItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query/Scan/BatchGetItem/BatchWriteItem/TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems call pushes real AWS/DynamoDB ConsumedRead-/ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits, SuccessfulRequestLatency, ReturnedItemCount, ItemCount and TableSizeBytes datapoints (derived from the actual request, never synthetic) into the shared CloudWatch core, on both the TableName and the TableName+Operation dimension sets — the same engine core/vpc_core.py's EC2 status-check metrics use. Alarms set on these metrics evaluate and fire for real; 'Create alarm' pre-fills the TableName dimension and alarm actions publish to the simulator's own SNS.

UpdateTable(ReplicaUpdates) really backfills a new replica with the table's current items and then mirrors every subsequent write/delete into it synchronously (same pattern as core/s3_object_core.py's S3 Cross-Region Replication); DeleteTable is genuinely rejected while replicas exist, exactly like real DynamoDB's 'replication group must be empty' guard.
A rebooted node drops that cluster's whole item cache rather than just its own share (Vyomi models one shared cache per cluster, not per-node partitions).

features.t: DAX cache engine (item cache + query cache)
x: The cache engine itself is real: read-through/write-through in front of the DynamoDB store (core/nosql_store.py) with record-ttl-millis/query-ttl-millis TTLs from the cluster's parameter group, LRU eviction sized by node type, and strongly-consistent reads genuinely bypassing the cache — proven in tests/conformance/test_dax_core.py by mutating the underlying table directly and showing a cache hit serves the stale value while ConsistentRead doesn't.

WarmThroughput is stored and described (default 12,000 read / 4,000 write units per second; a request can only raise it, status is always ACTIVE). Vyomi has no physical partitions to pre-warm, so it changes no behaviour.

Provisioned-capacity auto scaling is Application Auto Scaling for the dynamodb namespace: RegisterScalableTarget (Min/MaxCapacity, SuspendedState; a range that excludes the table's current capacity pulls the table inside it), DeregisterScalableTarget, DescribeScalableTargets, PutScalingPolicy / DeleteScalingPolicy / DescribeScalingPolicies and DescribeScalingActivities, for table and global-secondary-index read/write capacity. TargetTrackingScaling policies really scale: utilization is computed from the table's ConsumedRead/WriteCapacityUnits CloudWatch datapoints per one-minute period, the table scales out after 3 consecutive minutes above the target and scales in after 15 consecutive minutes more than 20 points below it, clamped to the target's Min/MaxCapacity, honouring ScaleIn/ScaleOutCooldown, DisableScaleIn and SuspendedState, and the new capacity is applied to the table (so throttling uses it immediately) and recorded as a scaling activity.

An Enabled event-source mapping on the table's stream ARN invokes its function with the real DynamoDB-Streams event for every INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE record. Delivery is synchronous, one record per invocation (BatchSize/StartingPosition/FilterCriteria are stored but not applied), and a failed invocation is not retried or sent to a DLQ.

The integration really replicates: DynamoDB table items / RDS table rows are copied into an in-process 'Redshift-lite' warehouse (sqlite) on every touch/query ('sync on read'), and the Redshift Data API (ExecuteStatement/GetStatementResult, CREATE DATABASE ... FROM INTEGRATION) queries it. The SQL dialect is SQLite's, not Redshift's; replication is poll-on-touch, not a continuous stream; no data filters, encryption or cross-account semantics; the warehouse is in memory and rebuilt from the sources on boot. A real Redshift/SageMaker lakehouse is not run.

There is no public DynamoDB API for reserved capacity and Vyomi has no billing or payment: a purchase is a record of the commitment (Vyomi-only service vyomi-reservations; read/write units in multiples of 100, minimum 100, 1 or 3 year term). Utilization is real arithmetic: reserved units vs the RCU/WCU provisioned on every PROVISIONED table and global secondary index in the account (on-demand tables are not counted); unused reserved units and units provisioned above the reservation are reported. Nothing is discounted or charged.
Account-level table defaults are not modeled; edit capacity, class and protection per table from its Additional settings tab.

features.t: AWS Backup vaults, plans, selections, jobs, recovery points, restore jobs, vault lock
x: Backup plan rules with a ScheduleExpression (cron/rate, UTC) really run from the shared scheduler tick (core/schedule_core) against the selection's explicit Resources ARNs, creating attributed backup jobs + recovery points, and recovery points past DeleteAfterDays expire. Offline: background loop; Nano: only while the page is open. Tag/condition-based selections are listed but not expanded; missed runs coalesce into one; ScheduleExpressionTimezone is ignored.
